source.original_text: For the original r=q+1 independent standard d-dimensional Gaussian columns and only2q+1<d, let Yi be the same literal closed-cutoff physical-row tensor matrices. Let Mi be each actual expectation under that original product probability measure and Zi=Yi-Mi. Let wi=cos((2q+1)theta_i), on the exact source midpoint grid. Every ordinary Zi squared and every ordinary (wi times Zi) squared is Bochner integrable. Both sums over physical rows of those actual matrix expectations have Euclidean operator norm at most2r(r+2)/d. This private implementation consumer covers only the centered and cosine-weighted variance comparisons; no concentration or main lower bound is included.

decoder_context: Fin n is the finite index set of natural numbers less than n. Natural numbers embed into real numbers in the usual way.

EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps a coordinate function as that vector and WithLp.ofLp recovers the same coordinates.

stdGaussian on finite-dimensional real Euclidean space is the centered Gaussian probability law with identity covariance. Measure.pi is the finite product measure with its product measurable structure.
Real.log is the natural logarithm and Real.sqrt the nonnegative square root. An if-expression with a real inequality uses that exact condition, including equality in a less-than-or-equal condition.

Matrix.vecMulVec u v has entry u_i times v_j. Matrix.kronecker A B has paired indices with entry A_(i,k) times B_(j,l) at ((i,j),(k,l)). Matrix multiplication is ordinary finite matrix multiplication, not entrywise multiplication. The symbol 1 is the identity matrix.

Matrix.PosSemidef A includes both Hermitian symmetry and nonnegative quadratic form for all finitely supported vectors; on a finite real index set this is ordinary symmetric positive semidefiniteness.

Matrix integrals use the complete Euclidean operator norm and the Bochner integral. Integrable means almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite extended-norm integral; it is an asserted output wherever displayed. The integral is totalized to zero when not integrable, so the explicit integrability outputs are substantive.

# Complete anonymous theorem reconstruction

This reconstruction is unabridged. Its only mathematical and evidentiary input is the supplied anonymous JSON packet, specifically its anonymous Lean statement and approved definition context. No source text, source identity, declaration identity, audit identity, proof, repository instructions, or other file was consulted. The packet exposes `compiled: true`; this is supplied metadata, not independently verified compilation evidence.

## The theorem, with every defined object

For every pair of natural numbers \(d,q\), where natural numbers include zero, assume the strict inequality
\[
2q+1<d.
\]
There is no additional hypothesis. In particular, \(q=0\) is allowed; the stated inequality implies \(d\ge 2q+2\ge2\). Write \(I=\{0,1,\ldots,q\}=\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\), \(J=\{0,1,\ldots,d-1\}=\operatorname{Fin}d\), and \(m=q+1\) as auxiliary notation for the finite index sets and their size. Each occurrence of an index inside a real-valued expression means its natural-number value embedded into \(\mathbb R\).

Let \(D=\mathbb R^d\), more precisely \(\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\,\mathbb R\,(\operatorname{Fin}d)\), with its Euclidean norm and Borel measurable structure. Let \(E=\mathbb R^{q+1}\), more precisely \(\operatorname{EuclideanSpace}\,\mathbb R\,(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1))\), with the same conventions. Let
\[
\Omega=I\to D,
\qquad
\mu=\bigotimes_{b\in I}\operatorname{stdGaussian}(D),
\]
with the product measurable structure. Thus a sample \(\omega\) consists of \(q+1\) vectors \(\omega_b\in\mathbb R^d\); under the probability measure \(\mu\), these vectors are independent centered Gaussian vectors with identity covariance. Equivalently, the real coordinates \(\omega_b(i)\), for \(b\in I\) and \(i\in J\), are independent standard normal variables.

Let the real scalar \(r\) be the real embedding of the natural number \(q+1\), and let
\[
r=q+1,\qquad L=2r+3\log(1000d).
\]
Here \(\log\) is the natural logarithm and \(d\) is embedded into \(\mathbb R\) in the scalar expression. For each \(i\in J\), let
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+1-\tfrac12)\pi}{d}
          =\frac{(i+\tfrac12)\pi}{d}.
\]
Let \(t_i:I\to\mathbb R\) be the deterministic coordinate function
\[
t_i(k)=
\begin{cases}
1,&k=0,\\
\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i),&k\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
The second branch therefore runs over \(k=1,\ldots,q\), and is empty when \(q=0\). The square root is the nonnegative real square root. For each \(i\in J\), let the random Euclidean vector \(\operatorname{row}_i:\Omega\to E\) have coordinates
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\bigr)_b=\omega_b(i)
\quad(b\in I).
\]
This is exactly the coordinate function wrapped by `WithLp.toLp 2`; recovering coordinates by `WithLp.ofLp` leaves these coordinates unchanged. In particular,
\[
\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2
=\sum_{b\in I}\omega_b(i)^2.
\]

All matrices below are real square matrices with both row and column index set \(I\times I\); their size is \((q+1)^2\) by \((q+1)^2\). Define the random matrix \(Y_i\), for each \(i\in J\), by
\[
Y_i(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac1d\,
\bigl(\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
\otimes\bigl(t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
&\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2\le L,\\[2mm]
0,&\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2>L.
\end{cases}
\]
The products inside the two factors denote outer products of their coordinate functions. The Kronecker product has the order displayed: the row-vector outer product is the first factor, and the \(t_i\) outer product is the second. The scalar \(1/d\) multiplies the whole Kronecker matrix. The zero in the second branch is the zero matrix. The cutoff includes its equality endpoint: a sample with squared row norm exactly \(L\) uses the first branch. Explicitly, for \(b,k,c,\ell\in I\),
\[
\bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac1d\,\omega_b(i)\omega_c(i)\,t_i(k)t_i(\ell),
&\displaystyle\sum_{a\in I}\omega_a(i)^2\le L,\\[2mm]
0,&\displaystyle\sum_{a\in I}\omega_a(i)^2>L.
\end{cases}
\]

For each \(i\in J\), let the deterministic matrix \(\operatorname{mean}_i\) be its exact expectation under the just-defined product Gaussian law, and let \(Z_i\) be the variable centered by that expectation:
\[
\operatorname{mean}_i=\int_\Omega Y_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega),
\qquad
Z_i(\omega)=Y_i(\omega)-\operatorname{mean}_i.
\]
The mean is this integral over the entire sample space, not a free matrix, a conditional expectation on the cutoff event, or an untruncated outer-product mean. The cutoff event has already been incorporated into \(Y_i\). The finite-dimensional, measurable truncated matrix variable \(Y_i\) is bounded for each fixed \(d,q,i\), so its Bochner integral is its ordinary finite expectation. No separately displayed integrability assertion for \(Y_i\) is an additional conjunct of the supplied statement.

Finally, define the deterministic real weights and the real scalar bound
\[
w_i=\cos\bigl((2q+1)\theta_i\bigr)
\quad(i\in J),
\qquad
C=\frac{2r(r+2)}d
 =\frac{2(q+1)(q+3)}d.
\]
The frequency is exactly \(2q+1\). The scalars \(r,L,\theta_i,t_i,w_i,C\) are fixed by the definitions, not existential choices.

## The four asserted outputs

With all the preceding definitions in scope, the theorem asserts the conjunction of the following four claims:

1. For every \(i\in J\), the matrix-valued function
   \[
   \omega\longmapsto Z_i(\omega)Z_i(\omega)
   \]
   is Bochner integrable with respect to \(\mu\).

2. For every \(i\in J\), the matrix-valued function
   \[
   \omega\longmapsto
   \bigl(w_i Z_i(\omega)\bigr)\bigl(w_i Z_i(\omega)\bigr)
   \]
   is Bochner integrable with respect to \(\mu\). Here each \(w_i Z_i(\omega)\) is scalar multiplication of the entire matrix by the fixed real number \(w_i\).

3. The operator norm of the sum of the unweighted second-moment matrices satisfies
   \[
   \left\|\sum_{i\in J}
      \int_\Omega Z_i(\omega)Z_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)
   \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
   \le \frac{2r(r+2)}d.
   \]

4. The operator norm of the sum of the weighted second-moment matrices satisfies the same bound:
   \[
   \left\|\sum_{i\in J}
      \int_\Omega
      \bigl(w_i Z_i(\omega)\bigr)\bigl(w_i Z_i(\omega)\bigr)
      \,d\mu(\omega)
   \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
   \le \frac{2r(r+2)}d.
   \]

Each product \(Z_i(\omega)Z_i(\omega)\) is the ordinary matrix square. In coordinates, its \(((b,k),(c,\ell))\) entry is
\[
\sum_{(a,h)\in I\times I}
  \bigl(Z_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(a,h)}
  \bigl(Z_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(a,h),(c,\ell)}.
\]
It is not entrywise squaring. The weighted integrand is exactly \(w_i^2 Z_i(\omega)^2\) by ordinary scalar multiplication and matrix multiplication. This is an elementary equivalent way to write the displayed weighted product, with no change to its integrability assertion or to its norm bound.

The norm is the complete Euclidean operator norm of a matrix acting on \(\mathbb R^{I\times I}\) with its Euclidean norm:
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=\sup_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Ax\|_2.
\]
All matrix integrals are Bochner integrals in this finite-dimensional matrix space with that norm; their entries are the integrals of the corresponding real entries. The integrability outputs mean almost-everywhere strong measurability together with finiteness of the extended integral of the matrix norm. They apply separately to every \(i\) and to each of the two displayed square-valued functions. The approved context defines a nonintegrable Bochner integral to be zero; the theorem's explicit integrability outputs establish that these second-moment integrals have their usual expectation meaning. Thus the last two assertions can equivalently be written
\[
\left\|\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\mathbb E_\mu[Z_i^2]\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C,
\qquad
\left\|\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\mathbb E_\mu[w_i^2Z_i^2]\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C.
\]
The sum is inside each norm. Both conclusions concern sums of actual matrix expectations, not a sum of norms or a bound asserted pointwise in \(\omega\). The only universally quantified parameters of the theorem are the natural numbers \(d,q\) satisfying \(2q+1<d\); each per-index integrability assertion quantifies over all \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}d\). All four conclusions hold together for the same defined objects.

## Seven semantic slots

**objects.** The natural parameters are \(d,q\) with the strict inequality witness \(2q+1<d\). The defined carriers are \(D=\mathbb R^d\), \(E=\mathbb R^{q+1}\), and \(\Omega=\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\to D\). The defined law is the product of \(q+1\) standard Gaussian laws on \(D\). The real scalar \(r=q+1\), cutoff \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\), angles \(\theta_i=(i+1/2)\pi/d\), coordinate functions \(t_i(0)=1\) and \(t_i(k)=\sqrt2\cos(k\theta_i)\) for nonzero \(k\), and vectors \(\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)_b=\omega_b(i)\) specify the random matrix \(Y_i\). This matrix is \(d^{-1}(\operatorname{row}_i\operatorname{row}_i^{\mathsf T})\otimes(t_it_i^{\mathsf T})\) on the inclusive cutoff and zero outside it. Its expectation defines \(\operatorname{mean}_i\), and \(Z_i=Y_i-\operatorname{mean}_i\). The remaining objects are \(w_i=\cos((2q+1)\theta_i)\) and \(C=2r(r+2)/d\). The complete explicit definitions and matrix entries appear above.

**domains.** The parameters \(d,q\) are natural numbers including zero; all stated scalar formulas take values in \(\mathbb R\). Spatial indices \(i\) range over \(\operatorname{Fin}d\), and vector indices \(b,k,c,\ell\) range over \(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\). The sample space has the finite product Borel structure and probability law \(\mu\) specified above. Each \(Y_i,Z_i\) is a function from \(\Omega\) to real matrices indexed on both sides by \(\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\times\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\). Each \(\operatorname{mean}_i\) is in that same matrix space. Integrals are Bochner integrals there, and norms are induced Euclidean operator norms, not entrywise norms.

**quantifiers.** For all natural \(d,q\) satisfying \(2q+1<d\), define the entire displayed collection of carriers, law, scalars, coordinate functions, vectors, and matrices; then assert the conjunction of two universal integrability statements and two scalar norm inequalities. Each integrability statement separately quantifies over every \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}d\). The norm statements sum over every such \(i\) and integrate over all \(\omega\in\Omega\) with respect to the single law \(\mu\). The variables \(\omega\) and matrix-coordinate indices are bound in the corresponding functions, integrals, and coordinate descriptions. There is no existential constant, random sample hypothesis, or additional external parameter.

**assumptions.** The only mathematical hypothesis beyond the types of \(d,q\) is the strict integer inequality \(2q+1<d\). In particular \(d\) is positive and \(q=0\) remains permitted. The Gaussian law, cutoff, weights, centering, and constant are definitions rather than extra assumptions or arbitrary inputs. Integrability of each of the two square-valued matrix functions is asserted as an output, not assumed. Equality at the truncation threshold belongs to the nonzero formula branch.

**conclusion.** For every spatial index, the ordinary matrix square of \(Z_i\) and the ordinary matrix square of its scalar multiple \(w_i Z_i\) are Bochner integrable. The operator norm of the finite sum of the expectations of the first squares is at most \(C=2(q+1)(q+3)/d\), and the operator norm of the finite sum of the expectations of the weighted squares is also at most the same \(C\). Each \(Z_i\) is centered by the actual expectation of the already truncated matrix \(Y_i\). In the weighted conclusion the scalar is squared inside the expectation: \((w_i Z_i)^2=w_i^2Z_i^2\). Both bounds are on the norm after summing the expected matrices.

**scopes.** All let-defined objects and all four conjuncts are inside the universal scope of the same \(d,q\) and the hypothesis \(2q+1<d\). The per-index quantifier of the first integrability conjunct applies to its unweighted integrand only, and the independent per-index quantifier of the second applies to its weighted integrand only. The matrix expectation defining \(\operatorname{mean}_i\) is over the full product law with \(i\) fixed. Each subsequent second-moment expectation fixes \(i\) before the outer finite sum. The cutoff comparison applies to \(\|\operatorname{row}_i(\omega)\|_2^2\) before forming \(Y_i\), and centering is performed after that truncation. The weights are deterministic and do not depend on \(\omega\). The norm encloses the complete finite sum of integrals in each of the last two conjuncts.

**constant_dependencies.** The real \(r\) is fixed as \(q+1\); the bound is fixed exactly as \(C=2r(r+2)/d=2(q+1)(q+3)/d\), with no unspecified multiplicative constant or additional dependency. The cutoff is fixed as \(L=2(q+1)+3\log(1000d)\), with exactly the coefficients \(2,3,1000\). The scalar normalization of \(Y_i\) is exactly \(d^{-1}\). The angles depend on \(d,i\), the coordinate functions on \(d,i,k\), and the weights on \(d,q,i\), with frequency exactly \(2q+1\). The same \(C\) applies to both norm bounds; there is no confidence level, tolerance, exceptional event, or unspecified distribution parameter.

/-! Actual source-experiment uncentered squared moments, arXiv2610.20492v1 C.2.
The original column-product law, physical rows and closed cutoff stay literal.
The shared positivity-integral node is used on a genuinely integrable pointwise
PSD majorant residual; no moment/positivity certificate is a source input. -/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.RealMatrixPositiveIntegral
set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixVariance

theorem actual_source_truncated_matrix_second_moments
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)
  (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => Y i ω * Y i ω) μ) ∧
    Matrix.PosSemidef
      (C • (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) -
        ∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ)
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)

  let ν : Measure E := stdGaussian E
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let R : E → ℝ := fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2
  let G : E → M := fun x => Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp x)
  let weighted : E → M := fun x => R x • G x
  let feature : Fin d → M := fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let S : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (t i k) ^ 2
  let K : Fin d → N := fun i => Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i)
  let α : ℝ := (r + 2) / (d : ℝ) ^ 2
  let B : N := α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i)
  let good : Fin d → Set Ω := fun i => {ω | ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L}
  let squared : Fin d → Ω → N := fun i ω => Y i ω * Y i ω
  let c : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => S i / (d : ℝ) ^ 2
  let tensor : Fin d → M →ₗ[ℝ] N := fun i =>
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N).flip (feature i)
  let scaled : Fin d → M →L[ℝ] N := fun i => c i • (tensor i).toContinuousLinearMap
  let W : Fin d → Ω → N := fun i ω => scaled i (weighted (row i ω))

  -- Canonical fourth moment, transported by the actual physical row map.
  have moment := FixedSpectrumRadialFourthMoment.actual_radial_fourth_moment_matrix
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change Integrable weighted ν ∧ (∫ x, weighted x ∂ν) = (r + 2) • (1 : M) at moment
  have row_law (i : Fin d) : MeasurePreserving (row i) μ ν :=
    FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw.actual_source_row_marginal_law hq i
  have actual_weighted_integrable (i : Fin d) :
      Integrable (fun ω => weighted (row i ω)) μ :=
    (row_law i).integrable_comp_of_integrable moment.1
  have actual_weighted_mean (i : Fin d) :
      (∫ ω, weighted (row i ω) ∂μ) = (r + 2) • (1 : M) := by
    have measurable_on_map : AEStronglyMeasurable weighted (Measure.map (row i) μ) := by
      rw [(row_law i).map_eq]
      exact moment.1.aestronglyMeasurable
    have transport := integral_map (row_law i).measurable.aemeasurable measurable_on_map
    rw [(row_law i).map_eq] at transport
    exact transport.symm.trans moment.2
  have W_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (W i) μ :=
    (scaled i).integrable_comp (actual_weighted_integrable i)
  have good_measurable (i : Fin d) : MeasurableSet (good i) := by
    dsimp only [good]
    exact measurableSet_le ((row_law i).measurable.norm.pow_const 2) measurable_const

  -- Both ordinary rank-one squares, retaining the actual row's own cutoff.
  have rank_square (v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ) :
      Matrix.vecMulVec v v * Matrix.vecMulVec v v =
        (∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (v k) ^ 2) • Matrix.vecMulVec v v := by
    rw [Matrix.vecMulVec_mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.vecMulVec_smul]
    congr 1
    simp [dotProduct, pow_two]
  have gram_square (x : E) : G x * G x = R x • G x := by
    have h := rank_square (WithLp.ofLp x)
    have radius_sum : (∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (x k) ^ 2) = R x :=
      (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq x).symm
    simpa only [radius_sum] using h
  have feature_square (i : Fin d) : feature i * feature i = S i • feature i :=
    rank_square (t i)
  have squared_as_indicator (i : Fin d) : squared i = (good i).indicator (W i) := by
    funext ω
    by_cases hω : ω ∈ good i
    · have hcut : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L := hω
      simp only [squared, Y, if_pos hcut, Set.indicator_of_mem hω]
      change ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G (row i ω)) (feature i)) *
        ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G (row i ω)) (feature i)) =
          c i • Matrix.kronecker (R (row i ω) • G (row i ω)) (feature i)
      dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, ← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul,
        gram_square (row i ω), feature_square i]
      ext a b
      change (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ *
        ((R (row i ω) * G (row i ω) a.1 b.1) * (S i * feature i a.2 b.2))) =
          c i * ((R (row i ω) * G (row i ω) a.1 b.1) * feature i a.2 b.2)
      dsimp [c]
      simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
      ring
    · have hcut : ¬ ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L := hω
      simp [squared, Y, hcut, Set.indicator_of_notMem hω]
  have squared_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (squared i) μ := by
    rw [squared_as_indicator i]
    exact (W_integrable i).indicator (good_measurable i)

  -- The actual untruncated majorant is a nonnegative rank-one matrix.
  have W_positive (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (W i ω).PosSemidef := by
    let x := row i ω
    let v : Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun a => x a.1 * t i a.2
    have rank_positive : (Matrix.vecMulVec v v).PosSemidef := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star v
    have W_rank : W i ω = (c i * R x) • Matrix.vecMulVec v v := by
      ext a b
      change c i * (R x * (x a.1 * x b.1) * (t i a.2 * t i b.2)) =
        (c i * R x) * ((x a.1 * t i a.2) * (x b.1 * t i b.2))
      ring
    rw [W_rank]
    exact rank_positive.smul (mul_nonneg
      (div_nonneg (Finset.sum_nonneg (fun _ _ => sq_nonneg _)) (sq_nonneg _))
      (sq_nonneg ‖x‖))
  have residual_positive (ω : Ω) :
      ((∑ i : Fin d, W i ω) - ∑ i : Fin d, squared i ω).PosSemidef := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    apply Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ
    intro i _
    rw [squared_as_indicator i]
    by_cases hω : ω ∈ good i
    · simpa [Set.indicator_of_mem hω] using (Matrix.PosSemidef.zero : (0 : N).PosSemidef)
    · simpa [Set.indicator_of_notMem hω] using W_positive i ω
  have W_sum_integrable : Integrable (fun ω => ∑ i : Fin d, W i ω) μ :=
    integrable_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => W_integrable i)

theorem actual_source_truncated_matrix_second_moments
    {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d) :
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)
  (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => Y i ω * Y i ω) μ) ∧
    Matrix.PosSemidef
      (C • (1 : Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ) -
        ∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ)
:= by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)

  let ν : Measure E := stdGaussian E
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let R : E → ℝ := fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2
  let G : E → M := fun x => Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp x)
  let weighted : E → M := fun x => R x • G x
  let feature : Fin d → M := fun i => Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i)
  let S : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (t i k) ^ 2
  let K : Fin d → N := fun i => Matrix.kronecker (1 : M) (feature i)
  let α : ℝ := (r + 2) / (d : ℝ) ^ 2
  let B : N := α • (∑ i : Fin d, S i • K i)
  let good : Fin d → Set Ω := fun i => {ω | ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L}
  let squared : Fin d → Ω → N := fun i ω => Y i ω * Y i ω
  let c : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => S i / (d : ℝ) ^ 2
  let tensor : Fin d → M →ₗ[ℝ] N := fun i =>
    (Matrix.kroneckerBilinear : M →ₗ[ℝ] M →ₗ[ℝ] N).flip (feature i)
  let scaled : Fin d → M →L[ℝ] N := fun i => c i • (tensor i).toContinuousLinearMap
  let W : Fin d → Ω → N := fun i ω => scaled i (weighted (row i ω))

  -- Canonical fourth moment, transported by the actual physical row map.
  have moment := FixedSpectrumRadialFourthMoment.actual_radial_fourth_moment_matrix
    (d := d) (q := q) hq
  change Integrable weighted ν ∧ (∫ x, weighted x ∂ν) = (r + 2) • (1 : M) at moment

    FixedSpectrumSourceRowLaw.actual_source_row_marginal_law hq i

    (row_law i).integrable_comp_of_integrable moment.1

      (∫ ω, weighted (row i ω) ∂μ) = (r + 2) • (1 : M) := by
    have measurable_on_map : AEStronglyMeasurable weighted (Measure.map (row i) μ) := by
      rw [(row_law i).map_eq]
      exact moment.1.aestronglyMeasurable
    have transport := integral_map (row_law i).measurable.aemeasurable measurable_on_map
    rw [(row_law i).map_eq] at transport
    exact transport.symm.trans moment.2
  have W_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (W i) μ :=
    (scaled i).integrable_comp (actual_weighted_integrable i)
  have good_measurable (i : Fin d) : MeasurableSet (good i) := by
    dsimp only [good]
    exact measurableSet_le ((row_law i).measurable.norm.pow_const 2) measurable_const

      Matrix.vecMulVec v v * Matrix.vecMulVec v v =

    rw [Matrix.vecMulVec_mul_vecMulVec, Matrix.vecMulVec_smul]
    congr 1
    simp [dotProduct, pow_two]
  have gram_square (x : E) : G x * G x = R x • G x := by
    have h := rank_square (WithLp.ofLp x)
    have radius_sum : (∑ k : Fin (q + 1), (x k) ^ 2) = R x :=
      (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq x).symm
    simpa only [radius_sum] using h
  have feature_square (i : Fin d) : feature i * feature i = S i • feature i :=
    rank_square (t i)
  have squared_as_indicator (i : Fin d) : squared i = (good i).indicator (W i) := by
    funext ω
    by_cases hω : ω ∈ good i
    · have hcut : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L := hω
      simp only [squared, Y, if_pos hcut, Set.indicator_of_mem hω]
      change ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G (row i ω)) (feature i)) *
        ((d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker (G (row i ω)) (feature i)) =
          c i • Matrix.kronecker (R (row i ω) • G (row i ω)) (feature i)
      dsimp only [Matrix.kronecker]
      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm, ← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul,

          c i * ((R (row i ω) * G (row i ω) a.1 b.1) * feature i a.2 b.2)
      dsimp [c]
      simp only [div_eq_mul_inv]
      ring
    · have hcut : ¬ ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L := hω
      simp [squared, Y, hcut, Set.indicator_of_notMem hω]

    (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω)) μ) ∧
    ‖∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, Z i ω * Z i ω ∂μ‖ ≤ C ∧
    ‖∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω) ∂μ‖ ≤ C
 := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let t : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * θ i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω →
      Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (t i) (t i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ :=
    fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let w : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i)
  let C : ℝ := 2 * r * (r + 2) / (d : ℝ)

  let N := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  have raw := FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixVariance.actual_source_truncated_matrix_second_moments hq
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => Y i ω * Y i ω) μ) ∧
    (C • (1 : N) - ∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ).PosSemidef at raw
  have first := FixedSpectrumSourceMatrixMean.actual_source_truncated_matrix_means hq
  have Y_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (Y i) μ := first.1 i
  have Y_positive (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (Y i ω).PosSemidef := by
    by_cases hc : ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L
    · let v : Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun a => row i ω a.1 * t i a.2
      have rank_positive : (Matrix.vecMulVec v v).PosSemidef := by
        simpa only [star_trivial] using Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star v
      have rank_eq : Y i ω = (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.vecMulVec v v := by
        simp only [Y, if_pos hc]
        ext a b
        change (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((row i ω a.1 * row i ω b.1) * (t i a.2 * t i b.2)) =
          (d : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((row i ω a.1 * t i a.2) * (row i ω b.1 * t i b.2))
        ring
      rw [rank_eq]
      exact rank_positive.smul (inv_nonneg.mpr (Nat.cast_nonneg d))
    · simpa only [Y, if_neg hc] using (Matrix.PosSemidef.zero : (0 : N).PosSemidef)
  have mean_positive (i : Fin d) : (mean i).PosSemidef :=
    integral_posSemidef (Y i) (Y_integrable i) (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (Y_positive i))
  have Z_hermitian (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (Z i ω).IsHermitian :=
    (Y_positive i ω).isHermitian.sub (mean_positive i).isHermitian
  have Z_square_positive (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) : (Z i ω * Z i ω).PosSemidef := by
    simpa only [(Z_hermitian i ω).eq] using Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (Z i ω)

steps.title: Center without assuming matrices commute
steps.text: Expand the ordinary square with both cross terms Yi Mi and Mi Yi. Fixed right and left multiplication preserve actual integrability and commute separately with the Bochner integral. The probability integral of the constant Mi squared supplies the remaining term. Thus each centered square is integrable and its expectation is the uncentered second moment minus Mi squared. Integrate PSD centered squares and add the PSD sum of mean squares to the already proved uncentered comparison.
steps.formula: \mathbb E_\mu[Z_i^2]=\mathbb E_\mu[Y_i^2]-M_i^2,\qquad A_i:=\mathbb E_\mu[Z_i^2],\qquad0\preceq\sum_i A_i\preceq C I_{r^2},\quad C=\frac{2r(r+2)}d.
steps.lean:
have expansion (i : Fin d) :
      (fun ω => Z i ω * Z i ω) = fun ω =>
        ((Y i ω * Y i ω - Y i ω * mean i) - mean i * Y i ω) + mean i * mean i := by
    funext ω
    dsimp only [Z]
    noncomm_ring
  have Z_square_integrable (i : Fin d) : Integrable (fun ω => Z i ω * Z i ω) μ := by
    rw [expansion]
    exact (((raw.1 i).sub ((Y_integrable i).mul_const (mean i))).sub
      ((Y_integrable i).const_mul (mean i))).add (integrable_const _)
  have centered_mean (i : Fin d) :
      (∫ ω, Z i ω * Z i ω ∂μ) = (∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ) - mean i * mean i := by
    rw [expansion]
    have hsub1 : Integrable (fun ω => Y i ω * Y i ω - Y i ω * mean i) μ :=
      (raw.1 i).sub ((Y_integrable i).mul_const (mean i))
    have hsub2 : Integrable (fun ω => Y i ω * Y i ω - Y i ω * mean i - mean i * Y i ω) μ :=
      hsub1.sub ((Y_integrable i).const_mul (mean i))
    rw [integral_add hsub2
      (integrable_const (mean i * mean i) : Integrable (fun _ : Ω => mean i * mean i) μ)]
    rw [integral_sub hsub1 ((Y_integrable i).const_mul (mean i))]
    rw [integral_sub (raw.1 i) ((Y_integrable i).mul_const (mean i))]
    rw [integral_mul_const_of_integrable (Y_integrable i),
      integral_const_mul_of_integrable (Y_integrable i)]
    simp only [integral_const, probReal_univ, one_smul]
    change (((∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ) - mean i * mean i) - mean i * mean i) +
      mean i * mean i = _
    abel
  let A : Fin d → N := fun i => ∫ ω, Z i ω * Z i ω ∂μ
  have A_positive (i : Fin d) : (A i).PosSemidef :=
    integral_posSemidef _ (Z_square_integrable i)
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (Z_square_positive i))
  have A_sum_positive : (∑ i : Fin d, A i).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => A_positive i)
  have mean_square_positive (i : Fin d) : (mean i * mean i).PosSemidef := by
    simpa only [(mean_positive i).isHermitian.eq] using
      Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self (mean i)
  have centered_sum : (∑ i : Fin d, A i) =
      (∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, Y i ω * Y i ω ∂μ) - ∑ i : Fin d, mean i * mean i := by
    simp only [A, centered_mean, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  have A_sum_upper : (C • (1 : N) - ∑ i : Fin d, A i).PosSemidef := by
    have h := raw.2.add (Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => mean_square_positive i))
    rw [centered_sum]
    convert h using 1; abel

steps.title: Weight by the actual cosine and bound the real operator norms
steps.text: For the exact deterministic wi=cos((2q+1)theta_i), the range of cosine gives 0<=wi squared<=1. The ordinary weighted square is wi squared times Zi squared, so its actual integrability and expectation follow. The residual sum of (1-wi squared)Ai is PSD. Both expectation sums are therefore full PSD matrices bounded above by C times the identity. Real continuous functional calculus places their real spectra in [0,C] and bounds their actual Euclidean operator norms. This is the private centered/weighted consequence, separate from P public uncentered conclusion.
steps.formula: w_i=\cos((2q+1)\theta_i),\quad0\le w_i^2\le1,\quad\mathbb E_\mu[(w_i Z_i)^2]=w_i^2 A_i,\quad\left\|\sum_i A_i\right\|\le C,\quad\left\|\sum_i\mathbb E_\mu[(w_i Z_i)^2]\right\|\le C.
steps.lean:
-- Weighting uses the actual deterministic cosine, hence 0 <= w_i^2 <= 1.
  have weight_le (i : Fin d) : (w i) ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
    have hi := Real.cos_le_one (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i)
    have lo := Real.neg_one_le_cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i)
    change (Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * θ i)) ^ 2 ≤ 1
    nlinarith
  have weighted_square (i : Fin d) (ω : Ω) :
      (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω) = (w i) ^ 2 • (Z i ω * Z i ω) := by
    simp only [smul_mul_smul_comm, pow_two]
  have weighted_integrable (i : Fin d) :
      Integrable (fun ω => (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω)) μ := by
    simp_rw [weighted_square]
    exact (Z_square_integrable i).smul ((w i) ^ 2)
  have weighted_mean (i : Fin d) :
      (∫ ω, (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω) ∂μ) = (w i) ^ 2 • A i := by
    simp_rw [weighted_square]
    exact integral_smul _ _
  have weighted_sum_positive : (∑ i : Fin d, (w i) ^ 2 • A i).PosSemidef :=
    Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => (A_positive i).smul (sq_nonneg _))
  have weighted_residual_positive :
      ((∑ i : Fin d, A i) - ∑ i : Fin d, (w i) ^ 2 • A i).PosSemidef := by
    have h := Matrix.posSemidef_sum Finset.univ
      (fun i _ => (A_positive i).smul (sub_nonneg.mpr (weight_le i)))
    convert h using 1
    simp only [sub_smul, one_smul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  have weighted_sum_upper :
      (C • (1 : N) - ∑ i : Fin d, (w i) ^ 2 • A i).PosSemidef := by
    have h := A_sum_upper.add weighted_residual_positive
    convert h using 1; abel

  -- The real matrix operator norm follows from real CFC and full PSD order.
  have C_nonneg : 0 ≤ C := by
    dsimp only [C, r]
    positivity
  have real_norm_bound (B : N) (hB : B.PosSemidef)
      (hupper : (C • (1 : N) - B).PosSemidef) : ‖B‖ ≤ C := by
    have hsa : IsSelfAdjoint B := hB.isHermitian.isSelfAdjoint
    have hlo : 0 ≤ B := Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr hB
    have hup : B ≤ algebraMap ℝ N C := by
      apply Matrix.le_iff.mpr
      simpa only [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using hupper
    have slo := (StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff_spectrum_nonneg (R := ℝ) B hsa).mp hlo
    have sup := (le_algebraMap_iff_spectrum_le (R := ℝ) (a := B) hsa).mp hup
    have hn : ‖cfc (id : ℝ → ℝ) B‖ ≤ C := norm_cfc_le C_nonneg (by
      intro x hx
      simpa only [id_eq, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (slo x hx)] using sup x hx)
    simpa only [cfc_id ℝ B hsa] using hn
  change (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => Z i ω * Z i ω) μ) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin d, Integrable (fun ω => (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω)) μ) ∧
    ‖∑ i : Fin d, A i‖ ≤ C ∧
    ‖∑ i : Fin d, ∫ ω, (w i • Z i ω) * (w i • Z i ω) ∂μ‖ ≤ C
  refine ⟨Z_square_integrable, weighted_integrable,
    real_norm_bound _ A_sum_positive A_sum_upper, ?_⟩
  simp_rw [weighted_mean]
  exact real_norm_bound _ weighted_sum_positive weighted_sum_upper
